Signed by the governor June 14, 2025, 10:30 a.m.

threshold_mw.value: no MW figure for the very large customer class: the Commission defines it for each utility by order by 15 December 2026; a data center is defined as a facility designed to have a load of 100 MW or more; the qualified large-scale data center fee starts at 100 MW of peak demand

cites.quote: By December 15, 2026, the commission shall establish by order the definition and appropriate characteristics of a very large customer class or subclass for each public utility providing electric service.
"Data center" means a facility that is designed to have a load of 100 megawatts or more

requirements.value: the Commission must establish by order, by 15 December 2026, the definition and characteristics of a very large customer class or subclass for each public utility, in a rate case or another proceeding; it may approve, modify or reject a tariff or electric service agreement between a utility and a very large customer

cites.quote: The commission may do this in a rate case under section 216B.16 for that utility or in another proceeding.

The commission may approve, modify or reject a tariff or electric service agreement proposed between a public utility and a very large customer establishing the terms and conditions under which the utility will provide electric service to the customer.

requirements.value: the Commission must consider how best to achieve that all costs attributable to very large customers not exempt are assigned to the very large customer class or subclass

cites.quote: (1) all costs attributable to the utility's very large customers not exempt under subdivision 3 are assigned to the very large customer class or subclass determined by the commission under paragraph (a);

requirements.value: no exit fee printed: the tariff or agreement must contain protections so other customers are not placed at risk for paying stranded costs of serving the very large customer

cites.quote: (3) the tariff or agreement contains protections necessary to ensure that other customers of the public utility are not placed at risk for paying stranded costs associated with the utility serving the very large customer; and

requirements.value: the electricity provided to a very large customer must achieve each benchmark of the state's electricity standards (216B.1691), shown by a utility plan to serve the load without asking to delay or modify the standards; existing, renewed or extended agreements and very large customers taking service before 2020 are exempt

cites.quote: (2) the electricity to be provided by the utility to a very large customer achieves each quantitative benchmark of the state's electricity standards under section 216B.1691

This section shall not apply to existing, renewed, or extended electric service agreements of public utility customers meeting the threshold of a very large customer, or to very large customers that have been actively taking electric service from the public utility prior to 2020.

requirements.value: an annual fee the commissioner collects from each qualified large-scale data center, by the peak demand the utility arranges to serve: 2,000,000 dollars for 100 to 250 MW up to 5,000,000 dollars for 750 MW or more, paid into the energy and conservation account

cites.quote: (a) The commissioner must collect an annual fee from the qualified large-scale data center, on a schedule prescribed by the commissioner and deposited in the energy and conservation account established in section 216B.241, subdivision 2a.
(4) 750 MW or greater

requirements.value: each public utility must offer an optional clean energy and capacity tariff for commercial and industrial customers by special contract, with participants paying all proportional costs of the new resources and no cost shifting either way

cites.quote: The commission shall require each public utility to offer a clean energy and capacity tariff for commercial and industrial customers.
(5) prohibit cost shifting from the participating customers to other utility customers or vice versa; and

laws.notes: Statewide law of dataset row xcel_plains-02 (Minn. Stat. 216B.1622, read there in Minnesota Statutes 2026); this entry adds the session law, the 100 MW data center definition (216B.02 subd. 11), the clean energy and capacity tariff (216B.1623) and the data center fee (216B.72). Minnesota Statutes 2026 show subd. 2 amended by 2026 c 88 art 1 s 91 (the cross-reference to subd. 1; same outcomes). A qualified large-scale data center is defined by investment (at least 250,000,000 dollars within 60 months, 297A.68 subd. 42(f)), not by MW. Effective date: the session law says each section is effective the day following final enactment (signed 14 June 2025); the date itself is not printed.

threshold_mw.value: not published

Long-term contract with the electric utility, cooperative electric utility, or municipal utility serving the geographic area where the facility is located, which ensures no costs to serve the facility are passed onto other customers of the electric utility
